questions.problem: Given the **orthonormal** basis $B=\{[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{26}} \\ -\frac{5}{\sqrt{26}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{\sqrt{26}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}\end{aligned}]\}$  of ${R}^{2},$ find $[x]_{B}$ if $x=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthonormal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=x\cdot {q}_{i}.$ Computing the components of $x,$ we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{26}} \\ -\frac{5}{\sqrt{26}}\end{aligned}]=-\frac{5}{\sqrt{26}}-\frac{5}{\sqrt{26}}=-\frac{10}{\sqrt{26}} \\ {x}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{\sqrt{26}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}\end{aligned}]=-\frac{25}{\sqrt{26}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}=-\frac{24}{\sqrt{26}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have 

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{10}{\sqrt{26}} \\ -\frac{24}{\sqrt{26}}\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.problem:
Given the **orthonormal** basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $\frac{{x}_{2}}{4}$, where ${x}_{2}$ is the second component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ 0 \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\end{aligned}]\},\,x=[\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{6} \\ 3\sqrt{6} \\ \sqrt{6}\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2},\,{q}_{3}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthonormal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=x\cdot {q}_{i}.$ Computing ${x}_{2},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =x\cdot {q}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{6} \\ 3\sqrt{6} \\ \sqrt{6}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =2\sqrt{2}+3\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{2} \\  & =4\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\frac{{x}_{2}}{4}=\frac{4\sqrt{2}}{4}=\sqrt{2}.
$$

questions.problem:
Given the orthogonal basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $3{x}_{3}$, where ${x}_{3}$ is the third component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 7\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\},\,x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3 \\ 6\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2},\,{q}_{3}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthogonal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=\frac{x\cdot {q}_{i}}{{q}_{i}\cdot {q}_{i}}.$ Computing ${x}_{3},$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{3} & =\frac{x\cdot {q}_{3}}{{q}_{3}\cdot {q}_{3}} \\  & =\frac{4\cdot 1+3\cdot 2+6\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4+6+6}{6} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
3{x}_{3}=3\cdot \frac{8}{3}=8.
$$

questions.problem:
Given the orthogonal basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $15{x}_{2},$ where ${x}_{2}$ is the second component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\},\,x=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -15\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthogonal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=\frac{x\cdot {q}_{i}}{{q}_{i}\cdot {q}_{i}}.$ Computing ${x}_{2},$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\frac{x\cdot {q}_{2}}{{q}_{2}\cdot {q}_{2}} \\  & =\frac{10\cdot 4+(-15)\cdot 3}{{4}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{40-45}{25} \\  & =\frac{-5}{25} \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
15{x}_{2}=15\cdot (-\frac{1}{5})=-3.
$$

questions.problem:
Given the orthogonal basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $5{x}_{3}$, where ${x}_{3}$ is the third component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\},\,x=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -7 \\ 6\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2},\,{q}_{3}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthogonal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=\frac{x\cdot {q}_{i}}{{q}_{i}\cdot {q}_{i}}.$ Computing ${x}_{3},$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{3} & =\frac{x\cdot {q}_{3}}{{q}_{3}\cdot {q}_{3}} \\  & =\frac{5\cdot 2+(-7)\cdot 1+6\cdot 0}{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{10-7+0}{5} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
5{x}_{3}=5\cdot \frac{3}{5}=3.
$$
